supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.notes: Get 25-OH vitamin D tested first; target serum 40-60 ng/mL. Pair with K2 if dosing >2000 IU daily.

supplements.name: Magnesium
supplements.notes: Glycinate or threonate forms are best tolerated. Oxide is poorly absorbed and laxative-only.

supplements.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
supplements.notes: Look for TG (triglyceride) form and a combined EPA+DHA total — not just fish oil mg. Refrigerate to prevent rancidity.

supplements.name: Vitamin K2
supplements.notes: MK-7 form has a longer half-life than MK-4; 100-200 mcg daily is plenty. Avoid if on warfarin.

supplements.name: Zinc
supplements.notes: Long-term dosing >25 mg/day depletes copper — add 1-2 mg copper if supplementing chronically.

supplements.name: Copper
supplements.notes: Required when taking >25mg zinc

supplements.name: B-Complex
supplements.notes: Choose methylated forms (methylfolate, methylcobalamin) if you have MTHFR variants or sensitivity to standard B-complex.

supplements.name: Vitamin C
supplements.notes: Liposomal or split dosing improves absorption above 500 mg. Megadoses (>2g) can cause GI upset.

supplements.name: Ashwagandha
supplements.notes: KSM-66 and Sensoril are the studied extracts — generic root powder is much weaker. Cycle off every 8-12 weeks.

supplements.name: Creatine
supplements.notes: Skip the loading phase; 5 g/day reaches saturation in ~4 weeks with less bloating. Monohydrate is the only form with strong evidence.

supplements.name: L-Theanine
supplements.notes: Stacks well with caffeine at a 2:1 ratio (200 mg theanine : 100 mg caffeine) for clean focus.

supplements.name: CoQ10
supplements.notes: Use ubiquinol (not ubiquinone) over age 40 — much better absorbed. Statin users especially benefit.

supplements.name: Probiotics
supplements.notes: Strain specificity matters more than CFU count. Refrigerated, multi-strain products outperform shelf-stable in most studies.

supplements.name: Curcumin
supplements.notes: Requires piperine or lipid formulation for absorption

supplements.name: Iron
supplements.notes: Only supplement if deficient. Test ferritin first.

supplements.name: Melatonin
supplements.notes: Lower doses often more effective. Short-term use recommended.

supplements.name: Collagen
supplements.conflicts_note: No major known interactions at typical doses.
supplements.notes: Take with vitamin C to support collagen synthesis. Hydrolyzed peptides (2-5 kDa) absorb best.

supplements.name: Alpha-Lipoic Acid
supplements.notes: R-ALA form is more bioactive than racemic. Take on an empty stomach away from minerals (chelates them).

supplements.name: Rhodiola Rosea
supplements.notes: Look for SHR-5 extract standardized to 3% rosavins / 1% salidroside. Best taken in the morning — can be stimulating.

supplements.name: NAC (N-Acetyl Cysteine)
supplements.notes: Take on an empty stomach for best absorption. May reduce zinc and copper over time — monitor if dosing long-term.

supplements.name: Selenium
supplements.notes: Toxic above 400 mcg/day — stick to 100-200 mcg. Brazil nuts (1-2/day) are a food alternative.

supplements.name: Berberine
supplements.notes: Split into 500 mg doses 2-3x daily with meals — short half-life. Don't combine with metformin without a doctor.

supplements.name: Lion's Mane
supplements.notes: Effects on cognition build slowly — 8-12 weeks for noticeable changes. Dual-extract (water + alcohol) products are most complete.

supplements.name: Glycine
supplements.notes: 3 g before bed improves sleep onset and quality. Tastes sweet, dissolves well in water.

supplements.name: 5-HTP
supplements.notes: Do not combine with SSRIs or MAOIs â€” serotonin syndrome risk

supplements.name: Acetyl-L-Carnitine (ALCAR)
supplements.notes: Take in the morning — can be stimulating. The acetyl form crosses the blood-brain barrier better than plain L-carnitine.

supplements.name: Alpha-GPC
supplements.notes: More bioavailable than CDP-choline but has a slight depressive mood effect in some users at high doses (>600 mg).

supplements.name: Apigenin
supplements.notes: 50 mg before bed improves sleep depth. Found naturally in chamomile and parsley but supplemental doses are much higher.

supplements.name: Astaxanthin
supplements.notes: Fat-soluble — must take with a meal containing fat. 4-12 mg daily; the most potent natural antioxidant by some measures.

supplements.name: Bacopa Monnieri
supplements.notes: Must be taken consistently for 8+ weeks to see full cognitive benefits

supplements.name: Beta-Alanine
supplements.notes: Causes harmless tingling (paresthesia) â€” split doses to reduce
supplements.conflicts_note: No major known interactions at typical doses.

supplements.name: Boron
supplements.notes: 3-10 mg daily supports hormone balance and bone health. Megadoses (>20 mg) can disrupt hormones in the other direction.

supplements.name: Caffeine
supplements.notes: Avoid after 2pm to protect sleep quality. Tolerance builds quickly.

supplements.name: Calcium
supplements.notes: Split doses; calcium carbonate needs food, citrate does not

supplements.name: CDP-Choline (Citicoline)
supplements.notes: Citicoline form raises both choline and uridine. Better tolerated than alpha-GPC at high doses.

supplements.name: Chlorella
supplements.notes: Choose broken-cell-wall chlorella for absorption. May bind to heavy metals — useful for detox protocols but check sourcing for contamination.

supplements.name: Chromium
supplements.notes: Picolinate form is best studied for glucose support. Effects are modest — diet and exercise matter more.

supplements.name: Cinnamon
supplements.notes: Use Ceylon cinnamon; Cassia contains coumarin which may harm liver at high doses

supplements.name: L-Citrulline
supplements.notes: L-citrulline malate at 6-8 g pre-workout raises arginine more effectively than arginine itself. Take 30-60 min before training.

supplements.name: Digestive Enzymes
supplements.notes: Take with the first bite of the meal. Useful for specific issues (pancreatic insufficiency, lactose intolerance) — not a daily multi-enzyme habit.

supplements.name: DIM (Diindolylmethane)
supplements.notes: Start low; can shift estrogen metabolism significantly

supplements.name: Elderberry
supplements.notes: Best used at onset of illness or preventatively during cold/flu season

supplements.name: Fenugreek
supplements.notes: May lower blood sugar — caution with diabetes meds. Body odor side effect (maple syrup smell) is common.

supplements.name: GABA
supplements.notes: Limited blood-brain barrier penetration; PharmaGABA form may be more effective

supplements.name: Ginkgo Biloba
supplements.notes: Avoid with blood thinners; standardized to 24% flavonoids and 6% terpenes

supplements.name: Ginseng (Panax)
supplements.cycling: Use for 8 weeks then take a 2-week break
supplements.notes: Korean (Panax) is stimulating; American is calming. Cycle 8 weeks on, 2 weeks off to avoid tolerance.

supplements.name: Glucosamine
supplements.notes: Sulfate form has stronger evidence than HCl. Allow 4-8 weeks for joint benefits; not all responders.

supplements.name: Glutamine
supplements.notes: Most beneficial for gut healing and high-stress states; healthy people get enough from diet. 5-10 g daily for therapeutic use.

supplements.name: Green Tea Extract (EGCG)
supplements.notes: Contains caffeine; take with food to avoid nausea. Avoid evening use.

supplements.name: HMB (Beta-hydroxy beta-methylbutyrate)
supplements.conflicts_note: No major known interactions at typical doses.
supplements.notes: Most effective in untrained, older, or catabolic states. Take 3 g daily, split into 3 doses around training/meals.

supplements.name: Holy Basil (Tulsi)
supplements.notes: Tulsi extract supports cortisol balance. Often combined with ashwagandha for adaptogen stacks.

supplements.name: Inositol
supplements.notes: High doses (12â€“18g) for PCOS; 2â€“4g for anxiety/mood

supplements.name: Iodine
supplements.notes: Test thyroid levels before supplementing. Don't combine high-dose iodine with thyroid medication without supervision.

supplements.name: Krill Oil
supplements.notes: Contains natural astaxanthin; phospholipid form may be more bioavailable for some people

supplements.name: Lutein & Zeaxanthin
supplements.conflicts_note: No major known interactions at typical doses.
supplements.notes: 10 mg lutein + 2 mg zeaxanthin is the standard combo. Take with a fat-containing meal for absorption.

supplements.name: Maca Root
supplements.notes: Gelatinized maca is easier to digest than raw. Effects on libido and energy take 4-8 weeks of consistent use.

supplements.name: Manganese
supplements.notes: Easy to over-supplement — most people get enough from diet. Excess is neurotoxic; keep total intake under 11 mg/day.

supplements.name: Milk Thistle (Silymarin)
supplements.notes: Standardize to 80% silymarin. Useful liver support but not a license to drink — protective, not curative.

supplements.name: MSM (Methylsulfonylmethane)
supplements.notes: Often stacked with glucosamine and chondroitin for joints. Sulfur smell/taste is normal; mix with juice if needed.

supplements.name: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide)
supplements.notes: Sublingual or liposomal forms may bypass intestinal degradation. Evidence in humans is still early — NR has more clinical data.

supplements.name: Phosphatidylserine
supplements.notes: Sunflower-derived is preferred over soy. 100-300 mg before bed lowers cortisol; morning dose supports focus.

supplements.name: Piperine (Black Pepper Extract)
supplements.notes: Increases absorption of curcumin by 2000%, resveratrol, and many other supplements

supplements.name: Potassium
supplements.notes: Most needs should come from diet. RDA is 4700mg. OTC supplements limited to 99mg.

supplements.name: PQQ (Pyrroloquinoline Quinone)
supplements.notes: Synergizes strongly with CoQ10 for mitochondrial biogenesis. 10-20 mg/day is the typical dose.

supplements.name: Quercetin
supplements.notes: Poor bioavailability; take with piperine or quercetin phytosome form

supplements.name: Resveratrol
supplements.notes: Take with piperine to improve absorption significantly

supplements.name: Saw Palmetto
supplements.notes: Standardized extract (85-95% fatty acids) is the studied form. Allow 8-12 weeks for prostate benefits.

supplements.name: Shilajit
supplements.notes: Use purified/tested form â€” raw shilajit may contain heavy metals

supplements.name: Spirulina
supplements.notes: Source matters — choose tested brands (heavy metal contamination is common in cheap spirulina). 3-5 g daily.

supplements.name: Taurine
supplements.notes: 3-6 g daily — much higher than the small doses in energy drinks. Excellent for cardiovascular and recovery support.

supplements.name: Tongkat Ali (Eurycoma Longifolia)
supplements.cycling: Consider cycling: 5 days on, 2 days off
supplements.notes: Look for standardized extracts (Physta, LJ100) at 200-400 mg. Cycle 5 days on, 2 days off to maintain sensitivity.

supplements.name: L-Tryptophan
supplements.notes: Do not combine with SSRIs or MAOIs â€” serotonin syndrome risk

supplements.name: L-Tyrosine
supplements.notes: Most effective during acute stress, sleep deprivation, or demanding cognitive tasks

supplements.name: Vitamin A
supplements.notes: Toxicity possible above 10,000 IU/day long-term. Avoid high doses in pregnancy.

supplements.name: Vitamin B1 (Thiamine)
supplements.notes: Benfotiamine is a fat-soluble form with superior absorption
supplements.conflicts_note: No major known interactions at typical doses.

supplements.name: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)
supplements.notes: Methylcobalamin or adenosylcobalamin preferred. Sublingual highly effective.

supplements.name: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)
supplements.notes: High doses used clinically for migraine prevention (400mg/day)

supplements.name: Vitamin B3 (Niacin/Niacinamide)
supplements.notes: Niacin causes flushing; niacinamide does not. High-dose niacin for cholesterol requires medical supervision.

supplements.name: Vitamin B5 (Pantothenic Acid)
supplements.conflicts_note: No major known interactions at typical doses.
supplements.notes: Generally well-tolerated. High doses (>1g) historically used for acne but evidence is weak.

supplements.name: Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)
supplements.notes: P5P (pyridoxal-5-phosphate) is the active form with superior bioavailability. Do not exceed 100mg/day long-term.

supplements.name: Vitamin B7 (Biotin)
supplements.notes: High doses can interfere with thyroid and troponin lab tests

supplements.name: Vitamin B9 (Folate)
supplements.notes: Methylfolate (5-MTHF) preferred over folic acid. Critical before and during pregnancy.

supplements.name: Vitamin E
supplements.notes: Use mixed tocopherols/tocotrienols rather than just alpha-tocopherol alone

supplements.name: Magnesium L-Threonate
supplements.notes: The only magnesium form that meaningfully raises brain magnesium. 2 g (144 mg elemental Mg) is the studied dose.

supplements.name: Reishi Mushroom
supplements.notes: Dual-extracted (water + alcohol) tinctures or extracts beat plain powder. Bitter taste — capsules preferred.

supplements.name: Cordyceps Mushroom
supplements.notes: CS-4 strain is most studied. Take in the morning — can be stimulating for some users.

supplements.name: Chaga Mushroom
supplements.notes: Wild-harvested can contain high oxalates — limit to 1-2 g daily if prone to kidney stones.

supplements.name: Turkey Tail Mushroom
supplements.notes: PSK and PSP fractions have the strongest immune evidence. Look for hot-water-extracted products.

supplements.name: Urolithin A
supplements.conflicts_note: No major known interactions at typical doses.
supplements.notes: Most people don't convert ellagitannins to urolithin A efficiently — direct supplementation bypasses this. Mitopure is the studied brand.

supplements.name: Ginger
supplements.notes: Standardize to gingerols. Effective for nausea and inflammation — 1-2 g daily extract or 4 g fresh root.

supplements.name: Moringa
supplements.notes: Nutrient-dense whole-food supplement. Don't use during pregnancy (root and bark especially).

supplements.name: Prenatal Vitamins
supplements.notes: Methylfolate (not folic acid) is preferred for women with MTHFR variants. Start 3 months before conception.

supplements.name: Tart Cherry
supplements.notes: Concentrate (1-2 oz) before bed for sleep and recovery. Higher dose pre-workout reduces muscle soreness.

supplements.name: L-Carnitine
supplements.notes: L-tartrate form is best for exercise recovery; acetyl form for cognition. Take with carbs to enhance muscle uptake.

supplements.name: Fisetin
supplements.notes: Senolytic dosing protocol is 20 mg/kg for 2 consecutive days monthly — much higher than daily-use doses.

supplements.name: Spermidine
supplements.notes: Wheat germ extract is the typical source. Effects on autophagy are slow — measured in months, not weeks.

supplements.name: Choline
supplements.notes: Most adults are deficient. Eggs are the best food source; supplemental choline bitartrate is cheap but less bioavailable than alpha-GPC or CDP-choline.

supplements.name: Carnosine
supplements.conflicts_note: No major known interactions at typical doses.
supplements.notes: Beta-alanine is a more cost-effective precursor for raising muscle carnosine. Direct carnosine supplementation is better for cognitive/longevity goals.

supplements.name: Maitake Mushroom
supplements.notes: D-fraction is the studied immune-modulating component. Hot-water extraction required for active polysaccharides.

supplements.name: Shiitake Mushroom
supplements.notes: Lentinan is the active compound. Culinary doses are too low for therapeutic effect — use extracts.

supplements.name: Hawthorn
supplements.notes: Can potentiate blood pressure medications — stack carefully. Effects on cardiac function build over 4-12 weeks.

supplements.name: TMG (Betaine)
supplements.conflicts_note: No major known interactions at typical doses.
supplements.notes: Lowers homocysteine alongside B12 and folate. 1-3 g daily; also a useful pre-workout for power output.

supplements.name: Red Yeast Rice
supplements.notes: Contains naturally occurring monacolin K (lovastatin) — treat like a statin. Pair with CoQ10 and avoid combining with prescription statins.

supplements.name: Pomegranate Extract
supplements.notes: Standardize to punicalagins (40%+). Supports cardiovascular and prostate health; juice is also effective but high in sugar.

supplements.name: L-Arginine
supplements.notes: Citrulline raises arginine more effectively than arginine itself due to first-pass metabolism. Skip arginine — use citrulline.

supplements.name: Schisandra
supplements.notes: Adaptogen supporting liver and stress response. Bitter — capsules preferred over tincture.

supplements.name: Gotu Kola
supplements.notes: Supports circulation, skin, and cognition. Triterpenes are the active fraction — look for standardized extracts.

supplements.name: Benfotiamine
supplements.conflicts_note: No major known interactions at typical doses.
supplements.notes: Fat-soluble thiamine analog. Much better absorbed than standard B1; particularly useful for diabetic neuropathy support.

supplements.name: Tribulus Terrestris
supplements.notes: Despite the marketing, evidence for testosterone elevation in healthy men is weak. May support libido through other mechanisms.

supplements.name: Horny Goat Weed
supplements.notes: Icariin is the active compound — standardize to 20%+. Mild PDE5 inhibition.

supplements.name: Nicotinamide Riboside (NR)
supplements.notes: Niagen is the patented, well-studied form. Raises NAD+ more reliably in humans than NMN currently does.

supplements.name: Multivitamin
supplements.notes: Choose one with methylated B vitamins and chelated minerals for best absorption.

supplements.name: Pine Pollen
supplements.notes: May cause increased libido. Pregnant women should avoid.

supplements.name: DHEA
supplements.notes: True hormone — requires baseline labs and ongoing monitoring. Most benefit is in adults over 40 with confirmed low DHEA-S. Avoid in hormone-sensitive cancer history.

supplements.name: Pregnenolone
supplements.notes: Master steroid precursor — affects every downstream hormone. Start at 10 mg; higher doses introduce hormonal side effects without added cognitive benefit. Strong PTSD adjunct evidence.

supplements.name: Fadogia Agrestis
supplements.notes: Cycle aggressively (8 weeks on, 4 weeks off). Rodent studies show liver/kidney toxicity at high doses. Limited human data — get baseline labs before use. Avoid under 25.

supplements.name: Pterostilbene
supplements.notes: 80%+ bioavailable vs 20% for resveratrol — methylated form is far more practical. One trial showed mild LDL elevation; monitor lipids. Pairs naturally with NAD+ precursors.

supplements.name: Dandelion Root
supplements.notes: Avoid in active gallstone disease — choleretic effect can cause painful spasms. Asteraceae allergy is the most common contraindication. Roasted root coffee is a pleasant daily option.

supplements.name: Artichoke Extract
supplements.notes: Standardize to caffeoylquinic acids or cynarin. 1200-1800 mg/day needed for cholesterol effects; 300-600 mg sufficient for digestion. Strong choleretic — avoid in gallstone disease.
